subject: alternative error values for estimating UERE

messages.author: abc5c1c2dec4769c
messages.subject: alternative error values for estimating UERE
parts:
Hi Chris,

In your Error Vignette, you mention alternative values that could be tested in the error model such as number of satellites and time to fix. Are these recognized/supported by as.telemetry? I've had no problems reading in GPS.DOP or GPS.fix.type, but haven't been able to get as.telemetry to recognize GPS.satellite.count or GPS.time.to.fix. Am I naming these incorrectly or are these not yet available in the current version of ctmm?

Thanks!

Christina

messages.author: abc5c1c2dec4769c
messages.subject: Re: alternative error values for estimating UERE
parts:
Actually, I think I've got this figured out  

Does as.telemetry automatically convert satellite counts to HDOP based on the relationship between them? You mentioned a correlation between these values in your AniMove course - are you applying that regression to estimate HDOP whenever GPS.satellite.count is the only value present?

And for time.to.fix, I was trying to specify more than one timeout in the as.telemetry argument because I have a testing dataset comprised of collars with different timeout settings. But it looks like I can only specify one timeout value within the as.telemetry function. If I just subset to a single collar or to collars with the same timeout setting, it works just fine.

Christina

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: alternative error values for estimating UERE
parts:
Hi Christina,

Using the number of satellites is (by default) a fallback model if no DOP value is detected in the data. I have a formula that automatically converts the satellite count into an approximate DOP value.
You can test whether or not this model outperforms your DOP values by importing the calibration data with and without the DOP column. The DOP values are supposed to be better, but sometimes they are garbage.
You can test whether or not either one of those models outperforms the homoskedastic error model by importing the calibration data without any of those columns.

Best,
Chris
